purpose: problems_found.md must stay in chronological section order. This has broken twice, both times from the same cause: appending with apply_patch anchored on the closing 'safety declaration + driver sha256' lines, which are boilerplate at the end of nearly every section, so the anchor is not unique, apply_patch matches the first occurrence, and the new section silently lands mid-file while the patch still reports success.

lossless_reorder_verification.method: reorder by splitting on '^## <TAG>. ' headings, stripping trailing '---' separators, then rejoining with a uniform separator; verified by multiset comparison of content lines

negative_tests.why: a check that only ever prints OK is worthless; each failure mode was injected into a COPY in /tmp and the check was confirmed to exit non-zero with the right diagnosis. The pack's own file was never modified for these tests.

cases.observed_output: problems_found.md: 84 sections (A..CF), 363 subsections / OK: chronological order, no duplicate headings, all subsections contiguous
cases.note: re-run after §CE and §CF were appended, so the section/subsection counts in this line reflect the current file; the four injection cases were run against copies of the file as it stood at 82 sections and their conclusions are unaffected, since each injection is a local edit whose detection does not depend on the total count

known_legal_exception: section BR numbers its subsections from BR.0 by design ('validate the projection before pricing with it'), so a .0 start is accepted and only gaps or duplicates fail. The first run of the check flagged BR as a failure before this was relaxed -- a false positive, not a real defect.
